Parcel
pär'sĕl
n. (a portion or plot of ground; a piece of land distinguished from the whole)
Old French parcelle, from Latin particula, a small part. In the Authorized Version it is almost always a parcel of ground, and the parcels it names are theologically weighted.

Biblical Definition

Jacob, coming to Shechem, “bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem's father, for an hundred pieces of money” (Gen 33:19) — a purchase in a land already promised to him, and he built an altar there. Centuries later: “the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought…and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph” (Jos 24:32). Joseph had made the children of Israel swear it, by faith, on his deathbed in Egypt, and the promise was kept four hundred years later in a field his father had bought. Then Boaz at the gate: “Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech's” (Rut 4:3) — and the kinsman-redeemer must take the land and the widow together, which is the whole doctrine of redemption in a property transaction. And a parcel of barley: at Pasdammim “there was a parcel of ground full of barley; and the people fled from before the Philistines” (1Ch 11:13) — and Eleazar stood in the midst of it and defended it, and the LORD saved them by a great deliverance.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a parcel as a portion of any thing taken separately; a part; a quantity or portion of land.

expand to see more

PARCEL, n. A portion of any thing taken separately; a part, distinct from the rest.

2. A quantity or portion; as a parcel of land.

3. A part belonging to a whole; as, part and parcel.

Key Scripture

Gen 33:19 — "And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem's father, for an hundred pieces of money."

Jos 24:32 — "And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph."

Rut 4:3 — "And he said unto the kinsman, Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech's:"

Modern Corruption

God's promises are habitually expected on a timescale of weeks, and Scripture keeps its largest ones across centuries and through deathbed instructions that outlive the men who gave them.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A parcel is a piece of ground. What the parcels teach is patience. Jacob bought a field at Shechem and pitched a tent on it. Joseph, dying in Egypt with a viceroy's honours, gave commandment concerning his bones — and Hebrews 11:22 lists that one act as the summary of his faith, not the coat, the dreams, the prison, or the throne. Four hundred years passed. A generation that had never seen Joseph carried a coffin out of Egypt, through the Red sea, forty years round a wilderness, over Jordan, and buried it at last in the field his father had bought, and the field became the inheritance of his children. There is no shortcut anywhere in that story. The habit of expecting God's promises on a short horizon is not new — the disciples asked, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? — but a culture of immediate delivery makes it harder to resist, and it produces both premature despair and premature announcements. Hebrews 11 says of the patriarchs that these all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them. The bones went in the ground at Shechem because a man believed a promise he was told plainly he would not live to see.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew chelqah (H2513), a portion or parcel of ground; nachalah (H5159), an inheritance; ga'al (H1350), to redeem, of the kinsman's duty.

expand to see more

Hebrew chelqah (H2513) — a smooth piece of ground, a plot or parcel; Jacob's field at Shechem, Naboth's portion, and the barley field at Pasdammim; Genesis 33:19, 2 Kings 9:21, 1 Chronicles 11:13.

Hebrew nachalah (H5159) — an inheritance, a possession by lot; what the parcel at Shechem became to Joseph's children; Joshua 24:32, Numbers 26:53.

Hebrew ga'al (H1350) — to redeem, to act as kinsman; the duty Boaz took up with the parcel and the widow together; Ruth 4:4-6, Leviticus 25:25.

Usage

"“He bought a parcel of a field…and built an altar” — a purchase in the land already promised."

"“Buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought” — a promise kept four centuries later."

"“Naomi…selleth a parcel of land” — redemption transacted at a city gate."
